title: CSK Land Livingstone in Four-Player Trade With Sunrisers Hyderabad
excerpt: Livingstone's fee is halved to ₹6 crore as Chennai swap Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis for two all-rounders before the IPL 2027 retention deadline.
body:
• Chennai Super Kings have traded fast bowlers Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis to Sunrisers Hyderabad for all-rounders Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards, the IPL confirmed on Thursday, November 5.
  • Livingstone joins CSK at ₹6 crore — less than half the ₹13 crore SRH paid for him — while Edwards moves at his existing ₹3 crore fee.
  • Khaleel returns to Hyderabad, where he played from 2018 to 2021, at his existing ₹4.8 crore fee; Ellis joins SRH at ₹2 crore.
  • The trade lands ahead of the IPL 2027 retention deadline on November 17, with the mini-auction set for December 16 in Goa.

Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad have completed a four-player trade ahead of IPL 2027, the league's organisers said on Thursday. England all-rounder Liam Livingstone and Australian seam-bowling all-rounder Jack Edwards move to Chennai, while left-arm fast bowler Khaleel Ahmed and Australian pacer Nathan Ellis go the other way, according to the IPL's media advisory and Reuters.

The fees tell the story

Livingstone is the headline name and the headline discount. Hyderabad signed him for ₹13 crore; he joins the five-time champions at a revised fee of ₹6 crore, a cut of more than half after a poor season. Edwards moves at his existing fee of ₹3 crore. In return, Khaleel remains on his existing ₹4.8 crore contract and Ellis joins Hyderabad at his existing ₹2 crore fee.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DfWmCW0R-JW/

What each side gets

Chennai buy batting power and flexibility: Livingstone is an established England white-ball all-rounder, and Edwards — who earned his first Australia cap after Hyderabad signed him — is yet to make his IPL debut, having missed the entire 2026 season with a foot injury. Hyderabad, in exchange, add two fast bowlers. Khaleel returns to the franchise he represented between 2018 and 2021; across his two-year stint with CSK he played 19 matches and took 17 wickets. Ellis, by contrast, appeared only once for Chennai, taking one wicket.

What happens next

The trade was completed with the IPL 2027 retention deadline approaching: franchises must submit their retention and release lists by November 17, and the mini-auction follows in Goa on December 16. Both squads' remaining auction purses — and how much of this swap was about freeing money for that day — will become clearer when the retention lists are published.

The arithmetic matters for both purses. Hyderabad signed Livingstone at ₹13 crore and now move him on at ₹6 crore, while Chennai take on a proven match-winner at less than half his last price — the kind of discount that only appears when a franchise wants a contract off its books before retention day. With Edwards also arriving at a modest ₹3 crore, CSK have added two all-rounders for a combined ₹9 crore, less than Livingstone alone cost SRH. Hyderabad, for their part, convert that batting depth into two fast bowlers at a combined ₹6.8 crore, reshaping the balance of their squad rather than its headline value. Which side reads better will depend on the December 16 mini-auction in Goa, where both franchises now shop with clearer gaps to fill.
